channel.title: ada-media
channel.description: Daily build notes from an open-source project in progress.

item.title: The case of the phantom panels
item.description: An empty note and a media window appeared without being asked, and neither could be dismissed. Today's fix: panels that only exist when requested — and the start of note deletion.
item.content:encoded:
An empty note and a media window appeared without being asked, and neither could be dismissed. Today's fix: panels that only exist when requested — and the start of note deletion.

  • An empty “Untitled Note” appeared unrequested and had no delete control; note deletion is now being added.
  • The media state said closed while a standalone media window stayed visible; the idle surface is removed so panels only appear on request.
  • The panel fix shipped front-end-only, with close, hidden-input and recovery checks and no forced headset refresh.

item.title: Ada drives Chrome from inside the headset
item.description: From VR, Ada switches Chrome tabs on the Mac, fills our YC draft and helps write the answers — while wireless ADB reconnects itself and failures stop going silent.
item.content:encoded:
From VR, Ada switches Chrome tabs on the Mac, fills our YC draft and helps write the answers — while wireless ADB reconnects itself and failures stop going silent.

  • From VR, Ada switches Chrome tabs on the Mac, fills the YC draft and verifies the form after reload without submitting.
  • Wireless ADB reconnects by itself at startup, with one bounded attempt and a fresh headset identity check.
  • Named movement works — “move Ada to the whiteboard” — while pointing moves fail with an honest explanation instead of silence.

item.title: Ada gets eyes
item.description: Screenshots from the headset land in a movable photo panel, the main window shows vision + ADB + room status at a glance, and Mac screen sharing gets a standalone, billboarded view.
item.content:encoded:
Screenshots from the headset land in a movable photo panel, the main window shows vision + ADB + room status at a glance, and Mac screen sharing gets a standalone, billboarded view.

  • Ada gets eyes: a fresh Quest capture of the real room, including passthrough and virtual content, in a movable photo panel.
  • Vision permission and wireless ADB become separate, measured states that expire when the connection goes stale.
  • Mac screen sharing becomes a standalone, billboarded frame with move, resize, close and independent near/far interaction.

item.title: Keep listening, and Ada learns to move
item.description: Hold an index finger up and pauses stop cutting my speech off; by evening Ada glides to the whiteboard on command with her ducklings trailing — and the daily log gets a repo that turns one note into posts for six platforms.
item.content:encoded:
Hold an index finger up and pauses stop cutting my speech off; by evening Ada glides to the whiteboard on command with her ducklings trailing — and the daily log gets a repo that turns one note into posts for six platforms.

  • Keep listening: holding a raised index finger through a pause stops Ada cutting speech off.
  • Ada relocates on command — “move to the server rack” glides her there with the ducklings following.
  • The message queue is now visible and editable, and deletion no longer requires an exact magic phrase.

item.title: The room becomes editable
item.description: Naming, relabeling and deleting the room around me — 8 surfaces deleted, 5 labels kept, saved as workspace revision 5 — plus worker cubes and speech that finally matches chat.
item.content:encoded:
Naming, relabeling and deleting the room around me — 8 surfaces deleted, 5 labels kept, saved as workspace revision 5 — plus worker cubes and speech that finally matches chat.

  • The room becomes editable: select, rename, relabel and delete surfaces. Revision 5 kept 5 labels and removed 8 surfaces.
  • Worker cubes appear beside Ada as real background tasks, driven by observations rather than animation.
  • Speech and chat finally match, streaming updates as they arrive instead of one block at the end.

item.title: Ada grows hands
item.description: Every WebXR hand overlay on at once — joint markers, radius spheres, aim rays, orientation lines — plus a cyan index-finger ray, the first developer preset, and the browser panel's first build.
item.content:encoded:
Every WebXR hand overlay on at once — joint markers, radius spheres, aim rays, orientation lines — plus a cyan index-finger ray, the first developer preset, and the browser panel's first build.

  • All WebXR hand overlays at once: joint markers, radius spheres, orientation axes and aim rays, plus a cyan index-finger ray.
  • The first developer preset saves the hand view to project memory; selectable presets are still missing.
  • The browser panel lands in code — Mac Chrome inside XR with video, audio and input — though the first live test still ends with an interruption.

item.title: Ada, take four
item.description: The fourth attempt at Ada starts here: the room imports, anchors and saves as a workspace — and the whole attempt gets logged in the open, one day at a time.
item.content:encoded:
The fourth attempt at Ada starts here: the room imports, anchors and saves as a workspace — and the whole attempt gets logged in the open, one day at a time.

  • First working room workspace: import the scanned room, align it, place a persistent anchor and save the layout.
  • A full reload restores the same room, with up to 64 named surfaces and 50 spatial notes.
  • Fresh-only capture: historical replay omitted, payloads capped at 48 KB, secrets redacted and the private outbox enforced.
